Possible cause: router.replace executes before clearAuth flushes, so the guard sees auth still present and immediately re-renders. Consider clearAuth() THEN router.replace.

Merchant nav inside the layout uses router.replace based on Zustand state. With Next.js persist + refresh_token cookie, full-page navigations can re-hydrate state from /api/auth/refresh; ensure the new token's user matches the stored user (assert sub matches) before treating it as still authed.

rca_of_the_issue: Hydration warning fix RCA confirmed: useMounted() gating in ConsumerHeader (city/cart badge), StickyBottomNav (wishlist badge) and ProductCardV2 (cart qty pill) defers Zustand persist-restored UI to client-only render, so SSR markup matches initial client markup. Reproduction: GET /product/prod-cf7a27405e in fresh tab, console clean. Reload x2, still clean. No remediation needed. For the session-loss artifact during cross-route merchant nav: the merchant layout's useHeartbeat hook + api client 401 interceptor can call /api/auth/refresh which reads the httpOnly refresh_token cookie (path=/api/auth). If a prior test registered a different merchant in the same browser context, that cookie still belongs to the older merchant, so the refresh succeeds with that user's identity and the Zustand store gets overwritten on next access. Mitigation: clear refresh_token cookie on /auth/login response when payload email != cookie owner, or always overwrite the cookie on every fresh login (it already does this — but only at path=/api/auth, so the old one is overwritten not deleted; this should work). Re-verify in a clean profile.
